children: Abivax named two new executives and said its loss widened in the first half of the year.
The French biotechnology company said Monday it appointed Chris Rabbat as chief medical officer and Tim Kelly as chief technical officer.
Rabbat, who has led global medical affairs since 2023, will succeed Fabio Cataldi, who is set to leave in the fourth quarter.

Kelly, who most recently was technology chief of Caribou Biosciences, will help advance commercial supply readiness and lead Abivax's chemistry, manufacturing and controls, as well as quality and information technology functions.

"As we prepare Abivax for its next phase of growth and the potential commercialization of obefazimod, we are continuing to strengthen the leadership and capabilities needed to support that evolution," said Chief Executive Marc de Garidel.

Abivax also published its financial performance for the first half of the year. It recorded a loss of 165.9 million euros, which is equivalent to roughly $190.2 million. That was wider than the loss of EUR100.8 million in the same period a year before.
Expenses increased for both research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative.

Research and development expenses increased to EUR107.9 million, up from EUR77.8 million the year before. That was mainly driven by new indications for its drug obefazimod, as well as higher costs from Abivax's Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis clinical programs.
Sales and marketing costs were higher as the company prepared for potential commercialization of obefazimod in the U.S.
General and administrative costs rose to EUR30.4 million from EUR16.3 million. The increase was due to an increase in personnel costs and consulting and professional fees.
